mechanism_narrative: A recovery in WORKPLACES after its sharp t-0w drop lifts weekday shopping trips within four weeks, because commuting generates incidental retail visits and lunch errands.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -5.6 at t-1w to -16.3 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC also weakened to -9.3
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains depressed or falls further and RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above 10 points, trip chaining shifts toward home-centered spending and suppresses discretionary retail visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 10 points and stays there for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 11.1 at t-0w and has been near 9-11 for four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior two-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases accessible daytime foot traffic, which pushes RETAIL_REC higher over the following month; the effect is strongest when both series move upward together.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -15.6 at t-0w and WORKPLACES was -16.3 at t-0w after prior weeks near -13 to -4
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve but RETAIL_REC is not higher than its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden deterioration in TRANSIT below -15 signals tighter mobility conditions that suppress nonessential retail access within one week and keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 points or drops by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -13.1 at t-1w to -15.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls below -15 or drops sharply but RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days, the threshold signal is false.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous easing in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates more routine local activity, which competes with discretionary mall trips and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -3.1 to -1.1 at t-0w while PARKS rebounded from -12.9 to -5.7
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS strengthen together and RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days, the hypothesized substitution effect fails.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS remains deeply negative, households are not substituting toward outdoor leisure, so retail demand stays weak over the next four weeks because discretionary outing intensity is still constrained.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -10 for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was -11.4 at t-2w and -12.9 at t-1w before rebounding to -5.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below -10 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not remain below its last-4-week mean over the next month, reject the claim.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM combined with stable RESIDENTIAL above baseline marks home-centered, local trip consolidation that diverts spending from retail-and-recreation venues over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved to -1.1 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL held at 11.1
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM improves while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: After a sharp WORKPLACES contraction, retail mobility weakens with a four-week lag because reduced office presence cuts weekday spillover traffic to nearby stores and food outlets.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops by at least 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -5.6 at t-1w to -16.3 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC also fell to -9.3
failure_condition: If a WORKPLACES drop of 8 points or more is not followed by lower RETAIL_REC within 28 days, the hypothesis fails.
